entries.reason: DXR Tier 1.1 is advertised only for the behavior-proven acceleration-structure, state-object, shader-table, direct/indirect dispatch, and tagged mixed triangle/AABB child-hit matrix. The M4/Metal provider now rejects unsafe heterogeneous Metal descriptor arrays and uses the explicit child-BLAS/TLAS compound path for the proven one-triangle/one-AABB shape; native heterogeneous BLAS, cross-process serialized reconstruction, and shader-table shapes outside that matrix remain unsupported.

Mesh Tier 1 is advertised for the behavior-proven source-owned AS/MS direct/indirect, 256-byte payload, layered depth/bounds/blend/wireframe, render-target-array, and PIPELINE_STATISTICS1 matrix. Work-graph execution, broader mesh payload/topology/resource shapes, and mesh per-primitive VRS remain explicitly unsupported.

The runtime now creates graph properties, reports local-root indices, validates a non-empty node-local-root table, and executes a bounded GPU-native reference kernel for three CPU-input and three GPU-input records without a CPU scheduler. Multi-node CPU/GPU routing, pointer-free record ownership, ordered dispatch reuse, malformed stride rejection, and bounded backing-memory overflow rejection have exact readback evidence. Recursive/fan-out graphs, multi-entrypoint resource/record routing, barriers, and general node shader conversion remain limited.

The compatibility provider creates video device, decoder, decoder-heap, and processor objects, reports one input stream, and round-trips descriptors exactly. A CPU-reference video-process command-list provider executes one RGBA8 input/output scaling shape through a VIDEO_PROCESS queue with exact readback. VideoToolbox codec execution, NV12/P010 conversion, profiles, metadata, and broader video queues remain limited.

Logical protected-session/resource association, status fence, lifetime, and CPU access denial are implemented and validated. The M4/Metal 4 provider does not claim hardware-secure protected memory, so secure protected capability remains unadvertised.
The stable DSR factory ABI and deterministic null-on-unsupported-device validation are implemented. No DSR device IID, scaling execution, or presentation provider is advertised.

A DXIL library creates a Metal linked-function pipeline with raygen, miss, triangle any-hit/closest-hit, procedural intersection/closest-hit, and callable exports. Stable identifiers preserve the Metal Shader Converter local-sampler field at bytes 16-23, keep alias hashes in the reserved tail, and execute a grown inherited hit-group alias through DispatchRays, including associated local-root constant and mirrored SRV/CBV reads, a mirrored sampler and static local sampler SampleLevel, and an exact UAV write from the shader record. Two filtered collections derived from one executable Metal table merge into a pipeline, reject a missing export, preserve renamed identifiers, survive every external collection release, and execute the full DispatchRays corpus. GPU-resident SRV/UAV/CBV and sampler descriptor-table mirrors execute through five 96-byte-stride local records; shader stack-size queries and configured pipeline stack-size retention are also behavior-proven. Independently linked collection merging, new-library growth, and complete stack/record-count/stride local-data shader-table matrices remain gated.

A four-byte AS-to-MS payload, object-stage root CBV and raw-buffer SRV, and object-stage dispatch pass readback; broader payload sizes, texture/UAV resources, barriers, and amplification patterns remain gated.

A bounded GPU-native reference node kernel executes three-record CPU/GPU input forms plus two-node CPU/GPU routing, pointer-free record ownership, ordered dispatch reuse, malformed-input rejection, and backing-memory overflow rejection. Source-owned `node_records` and three-entrypoint `node_multi` DXIL libraries are lowered at runtime into GPU-native Metal node kernels with exact CPU/GPU single-node and one-input multi-node backing-buffer readback, entrypoint routing, and a node-barrier witness. Resource/record fan-out, recursive graphs, cross-queue synchronization, and general node conversion remain limited.

A bounded SM50 provider now captures one or two non-rasterized DXBC vertex streams into independent output buffers and updates each filled-size location through ordered blits. Independent prefixes/counters and append accumulation are exact; overflow continuation, DXIL/geometry-stage capture, and downstream-consumer coverage remain unproven and stay fail-closed.

Native Metal placement-sparse backing now creates a 128x128x2 RGBA8-array reserved texture, maps both array slices through an explicit D3D12 placement heap, round-trips two exact 64 KiB tiles, and reads the same mapped physical tile through a second reserved texture. Native 1D R32_FLOAT arrays now map eight 16 KiB Metal pages, execute CopyTiles across both slices, and pass CopyTileMappings into an independent reserved array. A native reserved 3D RGBA8 volume now maps two 32x32x16 tiles, copies its mapping into an independent volume, and passes exact readback and physical-page ownership checks. A separate reserved two-tile buffer path uses an MTL4 placement-sparse buffer and D3D12 heap mapping on the proof host, then round-trips exact tile copies, copied mappings, and zero-after-unmap; focused R8_UNORM, integer/packed formats, BC1/BC4/BC7, standard-mip, and packed-mip CopyTextureRegion cases also pass. An explicit full shared backing fallback remains available when MTL4 is unavailable. The advertised Tier 3 report is limited to the 65-format behavior-backed provider matrix; formats without successful physical mapping/readback remain fail-closed. Standard and packed/partial-mip, 1D/2D-array/3D, cross-queue, alias, unmap-zeroing, and physical-page cases are covered by the stable resource probe, while unsupported format/provider combinations are rejected rather than promoted.

Named and unnamed buffers, upload heaps, fences, and inherited handle paths use pointer-free CreateFileMappingW metadata and pass independent-object plus cross-process read/write/signal checks. A committed shared RGBA8 texture uses a Metal MTLSharedTextureHandle Mach-port service and passes same-process and independent-process read/write validation. The D3D12 sharing-contract provider also records same-device resource presentation, capturable-work GUID lifetime, and shared-fence signaling. Non-shared texture shapes, window-backed capture, shared events beyond the mapped-fence bridge, and complete security/access-policy coverage remain unproven; those gaps must not be hidden behind the legacy in-process registry used only for unsupported object kinds.

entries.api: D3D12 geometry shaders outside proven emulation
entries.reason: Linked SM5 vertex/geometry AIR now executes through a Metal object/mesh pipeline and passes triangle readback. The Phase 7 corpus helper supplies four source-owned geometry fixtures that all create PSOs; broader topology, stream, resource, and captured-title coverage remains required before a general claim.

One behavior-identified hull/domain proof shape executes through native Metal tessellation and passes readback. General hull/domain shader conversion, patch layouts, partitioning/topologies, resources, and render-state matrices remain unsupported and are rejected rather than reported broadly.

purpose: Track explicit unsupported APIs so games are not misled by optimistic success returns.
